text: Given Essentials Admin credentials are sent, when tools/list is called, then the response includes the 4 proofpoint_essentials_* admin tools and all 6 proofpoint_essentials_threat_* tools, and still includes every pre-existing tool name.
Given Essentials Admin credentials for an org with domains, when proofpoint_essentials_list_domains is called, then the result is a JSON object with a domains list and no error key.

Given an org with more domains than one page, when proofpoint_essentials_list_domains is called with offset taken from a previous call's next_offset, then the next page starts exactly after the last record previously returned, with no record skipped or repeated.
Given Essentials Admin credentials, when proofpoint_essentials_get_user is called with an email that does not exist in that org, then the result's error.code is not_found.

Given Essentials Threat credentials, when proofpoint_essentials_threat_get_messages_blocked is called with no time arguments, then the result covers the last hour and is shaped like proofpoint_tap_get_messages_blocked's result (queryEndTime, counts, capped lists).
steps: Obtain a real Proofpoint Essentials Threat API Integration Key/Secret for a test org (none available to DEV01 at design time)
Start the server locally and send tools/call proofpoint_essentials_threat_get_messages_blocked with X-Proofpoint-Essentials-Threat-Key / -Secret headers and no time arguments
Compare the response shape against proofpoint_tap_get_messages_blocked's documented shape
expect: 200 response with queryEndTime, a counts object, and capped event lists in the same shape as the TAP equivalent tool; no error key
notes: No real Essentials account available at design time -- not a blocker per references/mcp-track.md 2.5. Covered at design time by mocked-transport unit tests and the documented API contract instead; this manual case runs once a real account is available.

text: Given a sinceSeconds value over 3600, when any proofpoint_essentials_threat_* tool is called, then the result is an invalid_argument error naming the one-hour limit.

Given no Proofpoint headers of any kind are sent, when any /mcp request is made, then the response is HTTP 401 and the body names all three credential options (TAP service principal/secret, Essentials user/password, Essentials threat key/secret).
Given only TAP headers are sent (no Essentials headers at all), when proofpoint_tap_get_all_threats is called, then it returns 200 with the same shape as before this change (regression guard).

Given only TAP headers are sent, when proofpoint_essentials_list_domains is called, then the result's error.code is not_configured and names the two missing Essentials headers; the gateway does not return 401.

Given only Essentials Admin headers are sent (no TAP headers at all), when proofpoint_essentials_list_domains is called, then it returns 200 -- the gateway does not 401 for a missing TAP header once another valid credential set is present.
Given Essentials Admin credentials that Proofpoint rejects (401), when any Essentials Admin tool is called, then the result's error.code is unauthorized and retryable is false.

Given two concurrent requests carry two different orgs' Essentials Admin credentials, when both call proofpoint_essentials_list_domains at the same time, then each response contains only its own org's domains, and neither request's credentials appear in the other's logs or response.
